backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, sample the initial radii from a distribution that favors larger values (e.g., a power-law or heavy-tailed distribution), while maintaining the SLSQP solver structure.
backlog.title: Multi-Start SLSQP with dynamic radii

backlog.spec: Start the SLSQP optimization with very small radii (making the feasible region large) and gradually increase the target radii during the optimization steps to 'grow' the circles into each other.
backlog.title: Gradual Radius Expansion

backlog.spec: Replace the hard inequality constraints in SLSQP with a penalty function: minimize -sum(r) + lambda * total_overlap_volume. Increase lambda over time.
backlog.title: Penalty Method instead of Constraints

backlog.spec: Instead of full random restarts, take the best solution found so far and perform several local optimizations starting from small perturbations of that solution.
backlog.title: Sequential SLSQP with local restarts

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initialization of centers with a Poisson Disk sampling approach to ensure initial circles are not heavily overlapping.
backlog.title: Randomized Initial Placement (Poisson Disk)

backlog.spec: Wrap the solve_once function in a simulated annealing schedule where the 'temperature' controls the acceptance of solutions with lower sum of radii.
backlog.title: Simulated Annealing Wrapper

backlog.spec: Implement a simple physical simulation where circles have velocities and 'bounce' off each other and the boundaries, while being 'pulled' by a potential that maximizes radii.
backlog.title: Velocity-based Gradient Descent

backlog.spec: Allocate more time to 'good' solutions. If a solve_once produces a sum of radii above a certain threshold, give it an extra 5 seconds of refinement time.
backlog.title: Variable Time Budgeting

backlog.spec: Use a barrier function (logarithmic barrier) for the non-overlap and boundary constraints to keep the optimizer away from the infeasible region.
backlog.title: Interior Point approximation

backlog.spec: Use the SLSQP result as a starting point for a Basin Hopping meta-heuristic, applying random perturbations and local optimizations repeatedly.
backlog.title: Iterative Basin Hopping

backlog.spec: In the repair step, instead of shrinking both radii equally, shrink the larger circle's radius more to maintain a more balanced size distribution.
backlog.title: Adaptive Repair Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Change the objective from maximizing sum(r) to maximizing sum(r^2) or sum(r^3) to favor larger circles, then switch to sum(r) for the final refinement.
backlog.title: Weighting Sum of Radii

backlog.spec: Start by placing the largest possible circles one by one greedily, then use SLSQP to optimize the resulting packing.
backlog.title: Greedy Circle Placement

backlog.spec: Fix the centers and use a coordinate descent (or a faster 1D optimizer) to maximize radii, then alternate with optimizing centers.
backlog.title: Coordinate Descent on Radii

backlog.spec: Apply a very high penalty for circles exceeding the [0, 1] bounds instead of hard constraints, allowing the solver to move through 'walls' to find better local optima.
backlog.title: Soft Boundary Constraints

backlog.spec: Use a simple SGD approach where the gradient of the radii sum is taken, and noise is added to the center updates to escape local optima.
backlog.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent with Noise

backlog.spec: Since the harness is single-threaded, use the time limit to run multiple short, fast optimizations instead of one long one.
backlog.title: Multi-threading Parallel Solve

backlog.spec: Incorporate a momentum term into the center updates during the SLSQP phase to help navigate through 'flat' regions of the energy landscape.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Updates

backlog.spec: Divide the unit square into a grid. Place circles randomly within cells to ensure a more uniform initial spread across the space.
backlog.title: Cluster-based Initialization

backlog.spec: In the repair step, calculate the gradient of the overlap and move centers slightly in the opposite direction while shrinking radii.
backlog.title: Curvature-based Repair

backlog.spec: Make the SHRINK constant adaptive based on the magnitude of the overlap found in the repair step.
backlog.title: Shrinkage Limit Scaling

backlog.spec: Solve the problem for n=25 first, then 'insert' the 26th circle into the best empty spot and re-optimize all centers/radii.
backlog.title: Successive Approximation

backlog.spec: Initialize some circles as mirror images of others across the axes to find symmetric optimal packings faster.
backlog.title: Mirror Symmetry Exploitation

backlog.spec: Initialize radii such that their sum is high but they are close to each other in size, then let the optimizer differentiate them.
backlog.title: Entropy-based Radius Initialization

backlog.spec: In the repair step, only consider overlaps with the 5 nearest neighbors instead of all $O(n^2)$ pairs to speed up the loop.
backlog.title: Local Search Neighborhoods

backlog.spec: Perform a small grid search or use a heuristic to set MAX_ITER more dynamically based on the initial overlap count.
backlog.title: Tuned MAX_ITER

backlog.spec: During the optimization, allow circles to slightly exit the [0, 1] box but penalize it, allowing them to 'slide' along the boundary.
backlog.title: Boundary Pushing

backlog.spec: Perform a very fast 'hot' optimization (high noise) followed by a 'cold' optimization (low noise) to settle into a deep local minimum.
backlog.title: Simulated Quenching

backlog.spec: Decrease the time spent on solve_once as the global best sum of radii increases (focus on refining good solutions).
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit

backlog.spec: Modify the objective to maximize sum(r) but add a penalty term that discourages any single radius from being too small.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Radius update

backlog.spec: Instead of discarding SLSQP results, take the best found (c, r) and perform 3-5 'hops': add a small random perturbation (e.g., 0.02 * std_dev of positions) to the centers, then run a short SLSQP with a smaller maxiter to find a local peak, keeping the best result across all hops.
backlog.title: Iterative Basin Hopping

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP step, perform a coordinate descent pass: for each circle i, try to increase its radius r[i] as much as possible while keeping it valid (no overlap with others, inside boundaries), potentially decreasing others slightly if necessary to make space. Repeat for a fixed number of passes.
backlog.title: Coordinate Descent on Radii

backlog.spec: Start by solving the packing for a smaller number of circles (e.g., k = n // 2) to get a good base configuration, then 'fill in' the remaining n - k circles by placing them in the largest remaining gaps, then run SLSQP on the full set of n.
backlog.title: Successive Approximation

backlog.spec: Modify the repair function to be more aggressive. Instead of shrinking both circles equally when an overlap occurs, shrink the smaller radius more significantly or shrink the radius of the circle that is most 'violated' (farthest from its neighbors).
backlog.title: Adaptive Repair Shrinkage

backlog.spec: Implement a dynamic time limit for `_solve_once`. If the first few SLSQP runs find significant improvements quickly, spend more time on the final best candidate. If improvements are stalled, end the run earlier to allow for more restarts.
backlog.title: Variable Time Budgeting

backlog.spec: Instead of hard constraints in SLSQP, use a penalty function: minimize -sum(r) + lambda * penalty_function(v), where penalty_function sums the squared overlaps and boundary violations. Gradually increase lambda from a small value to a very large value over multiple SLSQP steps.
backlog.title: Penalty Method with Gradual Hardening

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initialization with a Poisson Disk Sampling approach (or a simplified version) to initialize centers. This ensures that circles are spread out more evenly from the start, leading to a better initial configuration for SLSQP.
backlog.title: Poisson Disk Initial Placement

backlog.spec: Implement a simple first-order momentum update. After each SLSQP run, if the result is valid, take the difference between the new centers and the previous best centers. Use this 'velocity' to perturb the starting points of the next SLSQP run in the same direction.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Updates

backlog.spec: Add a small constant (e.g., 1e-7) to all radii during the SLSQP optimization to 'push' the circles against the boundaries, then perform a final high-precision repair to bring them back into the valid [0, 1] range.
backlog.title: Boundary Pushing

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP result, perform a local search: for each circle, try moving its center by a very small amount in 8 directions and slightly increasing its radius. If the move is valid and improves the sum of radii, keep it. Repeat 100 times.
backlog.title: Small Perturbation Neighborhoods

backlog.spec: Modify the optimization strategy to perform coordinate descent on the radii separately from the centers. After each SLSQP call that optimizes centers and radii simultaneously, perform a fixed number of iterations where only the radii are adjusted to maximize the sum while maintaining the non-overlap constraints (by scaling them down just enough to be valid).
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Radius Update

backlog.spec: Modify the objective function to include a small penalty for circles being far from the boundaries. In the packing of circles, the optimal configuration often has many circles touching the boundary. This encourages the solver to push circles outward towards the edges of the unit square.
backlog.title: Boundary Pushing Optimization

backlog.spec: Implement a multi-stage approach: first solve for n=10 circles, then use that result as the starting point for n=20, and finally n=26. This builds a dense packing incrementally. For the final step, you can start with the 20 circles and add the remaining 6.
backlog.title: Successive Approximation

backlog.spec: Instead of using SLSQP's hard constraints, use a penalty method where the objective is -sum(radii) + lambda * penalty. The penalty is the sum of the squares of the overlaps and the amount each circle exceeds the boundary. Start with a small lambda and gradually increase it (hardening) to force the solution into the feasible region.
backlog.title: Penalty Method with Gradual Hardening

backlog.spec: Instead of restarting SLSQP from scratch in every loop, maintain a 'velocity' vector for the centers and radii. Use the result of the previous SLSQP run to determine the next starting point, adding a momentum-based shift to explore the local landscape more effectively and avoid local optima.
backlog.title: Momentum-based Updates

backlog.spec: Implement a dynamic time budget. If the solver finds a new best packing quickly, spend more time on the next SLSQP run (e.g., increase MAX_ITER). If the solver is struggling to improve the best result, reduce the time spent on the current run to allow for more random restarts.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit

backlog.spec: Introduce a hybrid approach where, in addition to SLSQP, you perform a few steps of SGD on the radii. In each step, calculate the gradient of the sum of radii with respect to the radii (which is -1) subject to the constraints. Add a small amount of Gaussian noise to the gradients to help escape local minima.
backlog.title: Stochastic Gradient Descent with Noise

backlog.spec: Enhance the repair function. Instead of simply shrinking the radii of the two most overlapping circles equally, calculate the 'tightness' of the overlap. Shrink the radii of the circles that are 'most' overlapping or have the smallest current radii more aggressively to preserve the larger circles.
backlog.title: Curvature-based Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed INIT_RADIUS, sample initial radii from a distribution (e.g., truncated normal or power-law) that targets a total sum of radii close to the expected packing density. For each restart, vary the standard deviation of the radii to explore different size distributions. The goal is to find a starting point where the sum of radii is already large, reducing the work for the optimizer.
backlog.title: Multi-Start SLSQP with Dynamic Radii

backlog.spec: Instead of solving for 26 circles at once, solve for 1 circle, then 2, then 3, up to 26. At each step k, fix the centers of circles 1 to k-1 and only optimize the center and radius of the k-th circle. After a full pass of 26, perform a final global optimization pass on all centers and radii. This guides the solver toward a valid packing incrementally.
backlog.title: Successive Approximation (Circle-by-Circle)

backlog.spec: After a successful `_solve_once` result, perform a series of 'basin hops'. In each hop, apply a small random perturbation to all circle centers (e.g., 0.01 * standard deviation of current positions) and re-run the SLSQP optimizer for a very small number of iterations. If the new sum of radii is better, keep the new configuration. Repeat this until the time limit is nearly reached.
backlog.title: Iterative Basin Hopping (Refined)

backlog.spec: After the initial SLSQP solve and repair, implement a coordinate descent pass. For each circle $i$, keep the centers of all other circles fixed and maximize $r_i$ subject to the constraints that circle $i$ remains inside the square and does not overlap with any other circle $j$. Repeat this for all $i$ until the radii sums converge.
backlog.title: Coordinate-wise Radius Update

Start with a small $ho$ (soft constraints) to allow the solver to move through 'illegal' states to find better global configurations, and gradually increase $ho$ toward a large value to 'harden' the constraints and ensure a valid packing.
backlog.title: Penalty Method with Gradual Hardening

backlog.spec: For the first few restarts of the solver, enforce mirror symmetry (e.g., $x_i = 1 - x_{27-i}$ or $y_i = 1 - y_{27-i}$) by optimizing only half of the circles and reflecting the other half. This reduces the search space significantly and can help find structured, high-density packings. Relax the symmetry in the final optimization passes.

backlog.spec: Dynamically adjust the `MAX_ITER` for `_solve_once`. If a configuration is found that is very close to the current best (e.g., within 0.005), reduce the number of iterations to allow for more restarts. If a configuration is far from the best, grant more iterations (e.g., 500+) to try and find a high-quality local optimum.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit / Iteration Budget

backlog.spec: Enhance the repair step by using a simple force-directed approach. If circles overlap, calculate a 'repulsive force' between the centers of overlapping circles proportional to the depth of the overlap. Update the centers $c_i$ by moving them slightly in the direction of the force for several iterations before shrinking the radii. This moves the centers to 'make room' for the radii.

backlog.spec: Start by optimizing the radii with a very small $r$ (e.g., 0.01) and no overlap constraints, focusing only on packing them efficiently. Once a dense layout is found, gradually increase the target radii while introducing the overlap constraints as the objective function's penalty. This 'grows' the circles into the available space.
